name: Taming the Beast
summary: In Dun Morogh, Grif Wildheart tests your control of an Ice Claw Bear east of Kharanos. With an enchanted rod, you subdue the bear and learn to understand it. Then you earn the power to tame, call, and dismiss a lasting wild companion.

sections.title: The Strength of the Wild
sections.body: Dun Morogh’s mountaineers and scouts depend on hardy beasts in its freezing crags. You have practiced on swift, cunning predators. Now Grif Wildheart sends you to capture an Ice Claw Bear in the snowdrifts east of Kharanos. Its strength and endurance test the control every dwarven huntsman must learn.

sections.title: Earning a Companion
sections.body: The Taming Rod keeps the bear docile while you learn how wild instincts answer to will and calm intent. Your bond lasts only for the trial, which teaches discipline. Return the rod to Grif and the trials are complete. He then teaches you to pacify a compatible wild creature and call it throughout your life of adventure.

faq.q: What animal do I need to tame for this quest?
faq.answer: You need to tame an Ice Claw Bear in the frozen foothills east of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. The Taming Rod subdues it while you learn to handle its brute force.

faq.q: Do I keep the Ice Claw Bear after turning in the quest?
faq.answer: No. The Ice Claw Bear subdued by the Taming Rod is only a temporary test of discipline and skill. When you return the rod to Grif Wildheart, the bear departs, and you gain the abilities to tame any wild beast you choose.
Grif Wildheart is outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. He trains fledgling hunters in marksmanship and beast mastery.

faq.q: What abilities do I learn upon finishing this trial?
faq.answer: You learn Tame Beast, Call Pet, and Dismiss Pet. These abilities let you venture into the world with a permanent companion.

faq.q: What is the next step after completing this quest?
faq.answer: Grif sends you on to Training the Beast. There, you learn to feed, nurture, and instruct your new companion so it stays loyal in combat.

faq.q: Why does Grif have hunters test multiple types of beasts?
faq.answer: The three trials introduce different fighting styles: agility, cunning, and brute power. These temperaments help a mountaineer choose a companion suited to their hunting style.

angles.text: As a hunter, you begin as an isolated archer and become a true beast-tamer. You gain the essential abilities to tame and summon beasts.
As a dwarf, you know bears as favored companions of Dun Morogh’s mountaineers. They are renowned for matching their masters’ stubborn resilience.
